notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check (previous sweep 2026-10-31-b at 74112b4): four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, each result.json recording head d593bcb with uncommitted changes and skill_hash 1f3b1029..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, so the runs saw the working-tree SKILL.md. skills_listed is 40 (haiku-1, sonnet-1) or 53 (haiku-2, sonnet-2). Haiku-2 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md with Read; the other three read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, correct last-order dates (including a row with a +02:00 offset), the top five with ties broken by customer id, and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an amount with trailing text, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-1 raises FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because parse_amount/1 hands it straight to Decimal.parse/1, which no listed rule covers.

Rules changed since 74112b4, graded against the current text. On this case's list three rules changed. The with rule gained "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function": haiku-2 lines 96-97 and 105-106 nest the case for Decimal.parse/1 and DateTime.from_iso8601/1 inside a one-step with and are violated by that sentence and the one before it, while sonnet-1 (lines 131-132, 151-152, the shape the 2026-10-31-b sonnet-1 broke), haiku-1 and sonnet-2 put each such case in a private function. The do: rule gained "Put the value being checked on the left of `==` and what it is checked against on the right" and now says "function head" for the guard wrap; every == and != in the four files has the checked value on the left (haiku-1 147, haiku-2 90 and 136, sonnet-1 122 and 214, sonnet-2 91 and 100), so it moves no verdict. The -> rule gained "That pair stays inline because both rows return a value; when the success row calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, the clauses are not a table and every body goes below"; the only inline pairs are ones whose rows all return a value, and the one continuing clause (haiku-2 lines 62-63, the recursive parse_rows call) is already broken with its error clause, so it moves no verdict. Outside the list, Match every expected shape gained "Different failures need different reasons too: a caller cannot tell a missing field from a bad number when both return `{:error, :invalid}`", which is behind the haiku-2 entry under other_violations.

Verdicts worth checking. Haiku-2 line 98 ({%Decimal{coef: coef} = amount, ""} when is_integer(coef) -> {:ok, amount}, 74 characters) is violated under the -> rule as 2026-10-31-fable-test order-report-a graded the identical line; haiku-1 line 130's fn clause (71 characters) is held clean as 2026-10-31-b held the identical line. Haiku-2's Match every expected shape entry is new under the added sentence and a judgement: string_field/2 returns {:invalid_field, key} for a missing key, and the probe shows a row without "amount" and a row with "abc" returning the same reason; if the sentence is meant only for a bare {:error, :invalid}, the entry drops and no listed verdict moves. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 tell the two apart ({:missing_field, key} against {:invalid_field, key}), and haiku-1 returns :invalid_order for any missing key. Sonnet-2's case Enum.find(results, &match?({:error, _reason}, &1)) with {:error, _reason} = error -> error (lines 109-115) is held clean under the with rule as 2026-10-31-check-2 held the same shape. Sonnet-1's &(not Map.has_key?(row, &1)) (line 116) and defp completed(orders), do: Enum.filter(orders, &(&1.status == :completed)) (line 214) are held clean as 2026-10-30-check-3 held them. Haiku-1's Order struct without @type t is listed under the struct rule as 2026-10-31-b listed haiku-2's.

Result against 2026-10-31-b's skill runs: haiku 2 runs, violated on the with rule (0 of 2 before, 1 of 2 now), the -> rule and the pipeline rule (each 0 of 2 before, 1 of 2 now, haiku-2), clean on captures (1 of 2 before, 0 of 2 now; neither run uses a placeholder twice); sonnet 2 runs, clean on every listed rule, where 2026-10-31-b had sonnet-1 violated on the with rule and sonnet-2 on the Enum/Map rule. No opus run in a check batch, so the opus tier is unavailable.
